title: Finite-projective internal-Hom exchange on a stratum
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $g:S'\to S$ a morphism of schemes, and $a\leq b$, $c\leq d$ integers. Let $P\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be represented, on an etale covering of $S$, by bounded complexes of constant finite projective $A$-modules zero outside $[a,b]$; finite projective means a direct summand of a finite free module. Let $N\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ have cohomology only in $[c,d]$. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived tensor $\otimes_A^L$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and derived internal Hom $\mathscr H_T(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(U,V)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Scheme inverse images on these categories are exact constant-coefficient inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Then both $\mathscr H_S(P,N)$ and $\mathscr H_{S'}(g^*P,g^*N)$ have cohomology only in $[c-b,d-a]$, and the canonical map
$$\beta_{P,N}:g^*\mathscr H_S(P,N)\longrightarrow\mathscr H_{S'}(g^*P,g^*N)$$
is an isomorphism. The map is specified by
$$\mathrm{ev}\circ(\beta_{P,N}\otimes1)=g^*\mathrm{ev}_{P,N}$$
under the canonical identification $g^*(U\otimes_A^LV)\cong g^*U\otimes_A^Lg^*V$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

source.place: Tags 08DM (lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect) and 08DQ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex); agent constant-module ringed-site version and pullback evaluation/interval calculation.

proof.text: Refine the given etale covering so that on each chart U the object P is represented by a bounded complex E of constant finite projective A-modules in degrees [a,b]. The charts U'=U\times_SS' form an etale covering of S', and g restricts to g_U:U'\to U. The exact constant-coefficient inverse-image theorem [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] makes g^* and g_U^* exact, so g_U^*E is a complex of constant finite projective A-modules in the same degree range. Since restriction to a chart is inverse image along the etale morphism and g\circ j'=j\circ g_U for the chart maps j:U\to S, j':U'\to S', the monoidal composition comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] identify (g^*K)|_{U'} with g_U^*(K|_U) for every K, compatibly with the tensor comparisons; hence g^*P is represented on U' by g_U^*E and (g^*N)|_{U'}=g_U^*(N|_U). The restriction comparison for derived internal Hom [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies the restriction of each global RHom object with RHom on each localized chart; consequently the local models compute the restrictions of both objects in the claimed comparison.

source.place: Tag 0GM7, case (1), first paragraph: locality on the base and exact inverse-image of the local model

proof.text: On a chart choose any representative of N|_U and replace it by its good truncation F=\tau_{\ge c}N|_U; since H^j(N|_U)=0 for j<c, the truncation map is a quasi-isomorphism, and F^j=0 for j<c. Apply the bounded-free RHom-model lemma [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model] on U to (E,F), and on the inverse-image chart U' to (g^*E,g^*F): E and g^*E are bounded above with finite-projective terms, while F and g^*F are bounded below, so the ordinary Hom complexes represent the two derived internal Homs. The general chain map c_{E,F} of [lem-sf-etale-hom-complex-pullback] assembles the degreewise maps. For every term E^i and F^j, [lem-sf-etale-finite-projective-pullback-hom] says that this map is an isomorphism and carries the pulled-back evaluation to the evaluation after pullback. The finite direct sums in each total degree therefore give a chain isomorphism, and it is the local canonical comparison because it is induced by evaluation and currying.

source.place: Tag 0GM7, case (1), strictly perfect E and bounded-below truncation of N; Tag 08JI for the ordinary Hom model

proof.text: Put P^\vee=\mathscr H_S(P,A_S). By [lem-sf-etale-local-dual-interval] (with T=S, L=A_S, m=0) it is represented on the charts by the dual complex D=\mathrm{Hom}^\bullet_A(E,A) with constant finite projective terms in [-b,-a], and it has Tor amplitude [-b,-a]: \mathcal H^i(P^\vee\otimes_A^LM)=0 outside [-b,-a] for every module sheaf M in degree zero. P is perfect in the sense of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality] (locally a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free A_S-modules), so its canonical evaluation comparison P^\vee\otimes_A^LN\to\mathscr H_S(P,N) is an isomorphism. Since H^j(N)=0 outside [c,d], \tau_{\le c}N=H^c(N)[-c] and \tau_{\le d}N=N; apply the successive truncation triangles \tau_{\le n-1}N\to\tau_{\le n}N\to H^n(N)[-n] of [def-kun-truncations] for n=c+1,\dots,d. Tensoring each triangle by P^\vee remains distinguished by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated]; P^\vee\otimes^L H^n(N)[-n] has cohomology in [n-b,n-a] by the Tor amplitude, and the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives inductively that P^\vee\otimes^L\tau_{\le n}N has cohomology in [c-b,n-a]. Hence \mathscr H_S(P,N) has cohomology only in [c-b,d-a]. By step 1, g^*P satisfies the same hypothesis on the covering U' with models g_U^*E in [a,b], and g^*N has cohomology only in [c,d] because g^* is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; the same argument on S' bounds \mathscr H_{S'}(g^*P,g^*N).

source.place: Tag 0GM7, case (1), with the bounded cohomology interval obtained by finite truncation and the long exact cohomology sequence

proof.text: The local chain isomorphisms in step 2 agree on refinements: the RHom restriction comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] together with the evaluation and transpose restriction identities of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose] identifies every refinement with the same canonical map. Choose representatives and take cohomology; exact inverse image from [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies the cohomology of a restriction with the restriction of the cohomology. Each cohomology-sheaf map of the global map beta (step 5) is an isomorphism on the covering localized charts U', so [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] makes it an isomorphism globally; a map of complexes inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves is an isomorphism in D(S'_{\mathrm{et}},A).

source.place: Tag 0GM7, case (1), final locality and gluing step; slice evaluation-transpose compatibility

proof.text: The derived evaluation and transpose are those of the closed structure of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]: a morphism u:T\to\mathscr H(L,M) corresponds to \mathrm{ev}\circ(u\otimes1_L), so beta_{P,N} is the unique morphism with \mathrm{ev}\circ(\beta\otimes1)=g^*\mathrm{ev}_{P,N} after the identification of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. On a chart, with the representative normalization of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] and the representative evaluation of [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation], the derived evaluation on \mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I(F))\otimes E is represented (after a K-flat replacement of the first factor; E is bounded with flat terms) by componentwise evaluation x\otimes y\mapsto\phi(x)(y); the bounded-free model map \mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I(F)) of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model] is induced by F\to I(F) and so commutes with componentwise evaluation. The same holds on U' for g_U^*E and g_U^*F. The map c_{E,F} of [lem-sf-etale-hom-complex-pullback] is defined by currying the pulled-back termwise evaluation, and [lem-sf-etale-finite-projective-pullback-hom] makes the evaluation square commute on each E^i and F^j; summing the finitely many bidegrees and representing the tensor pullback comparison termwise on these K-flat models [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives \mathrm{ev}\circ(Q(c_{E,F})\otimes1)=g_U^*\mathrm{ev} on U'. By uniqueness of transposes Q(c_{E,F}) represents the restriction of beta to U', using the restriction identities of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose] and step 1 to identify restriction of the global evaluation and transpose with the chart ones. Thus beta is the evaluation-induced comparison of the statement, and step 2 shows it is a chart-wise isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Follows Stacks Tag 0GM7(1) on each chart with a strictly perfect finite-projective complex E and the good truncation F=tau_{>=c}N, using the bounded-free Hom model (08JI) on the chart and its inverse image. Added one statement-only node for the finite-projective pullback-Hom identity with its evaluation compatibility. The interval bound is obtained globally from the Tor amplitude of the dual and perfect duality; the identification of the chain map with beta uses the closed-structure transpose and the representative evaluation normalization; cover-local gluing is non-elementary. Maintainer FIX (2026-10-18): cited perfect duality and defined D in step 3, replaced the unsupported perfect-duality citation in step 5 by the closed structure and Hom-model normalization nodes, and cited the inverse-image composition comparison in step 1. The statement and all hypotheses are unchanged.
